drafting_notes:
AUDIENCE: Year 1 (ages 6-7). Frames 6-12 words, everyday scenes.
ANCHORS are sun position, meals and routines: first light and waking (morning), the sun at its very highest and lunch (midday), after lunch and school pickup (afternoon), the sky turning orange and tea on the table (evening), stars out and everyone asleep (night). Australian register: 'tea' for the evening meal is fine; January is summer.
PREPOSITION TRAP: English says 'in the morning' but 'at midday' and 'at night'. NEVER hang a frame on a preposition that only fits some members. Safe slots where all five nouns scan: the noun as subject ('___ settled over the farm'), after 'until', 'before' or 'by' ('by ___ the washing was dry'), or 'the ___' plus a verb phrase. Test all five words in the exact slot before writing the sentence.
SECOND-FIT TRAPS: evening vs night (evening still has some light and people are up; night is full dark and sleep); morning vs midday (morning is waking and starting; midday is the peak, lunch, shortest shadows).
SURFACES: singular bare noun for every candidate, the word itself, in every frame.

contrasts.line: Morning has first light and waking. Midday has the sun highest and lunch.
Morning is when the house wakes. Afternoon comes after lunch and school pickup.
Morning opens with breakfast. Evening has orange sky and tea.
Morning has waking and school shoes. Night has stars and sleeping.
Midday has the sun highest and lunch. Morning has first light and waking.
Midday is lunch with the sun highest. Afternoon is after lunch and pickup.
Midday has the shortest shadows. Evening has orange sky and tea.
Midday is bright lunch hour. Night has stars, moon, and sleeping.
Afternoon comes after lunch. Morning has waking, breakfast, and school starting.
Afternoon is after lunch and lessons. Midday has lunch and the highest sun.
Afternoon has pickup after lessons. Evening has tea and orange sky.
Afternoon still has play after school. Night has sleeping under stars.
Evening has tea and orange sky. Morning has first light and breakfast.
Evening has lamps and tea. Midday has lunch with the sun highest.
Evening comes with tea and baths. Afternoon has pickup after lessons.
Evening is before sleep, with lamps on. Night has everyone asleep.
Night has stars and sleeping. Morning has waking and breakfast.
Night has moonlight and quiet beds. Midday has lunch and the highest sun.
Night has sleeping houses. Afternoon has after-lunch play and pickup.
Night is full of sleep and stars. Evening still has tea and lamps.

meta.scrub_note: Scrubbed by claude 2026-07-10: all 40 read. Restaged 20 time-noun-as-agent personifications ('Morning put clean teeth by the door') into parity-safe slots; kept the storybook-legal ones (brought/came/settled/painted/wrapped). Midday frames re-anchored on sun position and shortest shadows, evening on tea and pink sky, night on sleep. Post-judge fixes s24, s31: trailing-adverb rejections, an evening/night co-fit (3-of-3), a now-crossing, and a warm-afternoon leak re-anchored (clock time, homework marker, will-future, span subject).
